title: Research: if the reported ETH disproof holds, no κ record moves; Alman–Li's depth-2 WHT barrier survives on OVC; what falls, what survives and what might open up (no new κ)
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

Adds one package, `research/eth-claim-fft-impact`: a map of what OpenAI's reported disproof of the Exponential Time
Hypothesis (preprint of 26 October 2026, under examination by a working group led by Russell Impagliazzo,
Ramamohan Paturi and Ryan Williams) would change for multiplication, the DFT and the WHT, **if the claim holds**.
It is an audit of conditional results, not a construction or a proof. No new κ; no record, target or frozen
package changes.

| Finding, if the claim holds | Status |
|---|---|
| No selected or historical κ record moves; I found no κ record, target, certificate or framework assumption on the hub that uses ETH, SETH or the Orthogonal Vectors Conjecture (OVC) | argued by hand; search limits in README Sources |
| ETH, SETH, Gap-ETH, NSETH, #ETH and their randomized versions fall, plus some lower bounds outside the FFT world that the algorithm beats directly (e.g. "no 2^(o(v))" for colouring; Curticapean's perfect-matching bound) | follows if the claim holds |
| Every theorem stands: the unconditional lower bounds, the non-rigidity and fast-transform results, my Lean-checked savings (1.7887045e-3 DFT, 1.5699306e-3 WHT) | theorem |
| Afshani–Freksen–Kamma–Larsen's Ω(n log n) rests on the Li–Li network-coding conjecture, not on ETH | conditional on Li–Li; unaffected by this claim |
| Alman–Li's "no near-linear depth-2 WHT circuit" loses its SETH leg and stands on OVC alone (their proof needs only that #OV in dimension O(log N) is not in N^(1+o(1))); OVC is not refuted by any known reduction but loses its usual derivation from SETH | conditional on OVC; argued by hand |
| SETH-based Subset Sum (Abboud–Bringmann–Hermelin–Shabtay), ETH-based k-SUM (Pătraşcu–Williams) and the NSETH barrier lose their basis without being refuted | follows if the claim holds; partly recalled |
| Williams 2013 Thm 6.1 fires (E^NP ⊄ SIZE(O(n))), plus the preprint's c·n·√(log n) corollary for one E^NP language, which needs the appendix-only sparse bound; nothing aimed at transforms, no rigid matrix, no linear-circuit bound | follows if the claim holds; argued by hand |
| No practical speed-up: with constants set to 1 the exponent factor is 0.73 at n = 10^4; the sharper exponent beats 1.307^n only beyond about n = 10^79 | computed (verify.py) |
| Speculation: whether the preprint's interpolation parameters improve the polynomial behind Alman–Williams / Alman–Guan–Padaki rigidity upper bounds; whether its tensor-contraction theorem can count orthogonal vectors after a low-degree split (the direct encoding breaks its degree cap) | speculation |

Remaining obligations: the claim itself (the working group's examination); the results marked "recalled" in the
README were not re-read; the hub search used a local copy from 22 October plus GitHub search, which can miss files;
no person has reviewed the map (one AI reviewer attacked every step).

## Task and overlap

- Base `de5ec2e7a6074068452f45b1a191b5c72832df4a`, priority revision 8. Card `scope-navigation` (method "Index one
  tightly related family of obstructions with explicit excluded and open hypotheses"), `scope_status: refined`:
  the family is the conditional results touching the ETH family, and every entry is conditional on an outside claim
  under review. Reason in `TASK.json`.
- No live inputs. Provenance rows: the task catalogue and `certificates/selected-result.json` (κ = 62009/20000000).
- Nearest work: #5813 and #5815 (Dugongue) carry the preprint's techniques to the Gaussian axis and claim no κ; this
  package adds the map of which conditional results move, and links them instead of repeating them. #634
  (ShikeChen01) and discussion #2838 (philippeVV) cover the network-coding side; this package only cross-references
  them. I found no hub package or discussion that maps ETH, SETH or OVC; that is a search result, not a proof of
  novelty.

## Validation

```sh
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/eth-claim-fft-impact --check-only
python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/eth-claim-fft-impact
# = python3 -B research/eth-claim-fft-impact/verify.py   (PASS_ETH_CLAIM_FFT_IMPACT)
python3 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/eth-claim-fft-impact
```

Standard library only. `verify.py` passes with Python 3.12.13 and 3.9.6 on an Apple M4 (macOS) in about 0.03 s and
19 MB, and leaves no files behind. It recomputes the five figures of README section 5 (0.7316, 0.7064 and 0.5096
for the exponent factor at n = 10^4, 10^6 and 10^30; 10^78.7 and 10^2390.2 for the two thresholds), checks that the
README prints each one, and rejects four false figures as failure controls. Everything else is a reading of sources
or an argument by hand, labelled as such. Not run: the card's first step (`scripts/research_selected_baseline.py`),
the preprint's Lean build, and any check of the preprint's proofs.

## Credit

OpenAI for the preprint (no individual authors named) and the working group led by Impagliazzo, Paturi and
Williams for the examination. Josh Alman and Baitian Li; Afshani, Freksen, Kamma and Larsen; Ryan Williams; Jahanjou,
Miles and Viola; Alman and Williams; Dvir and Liu; Alman, Guan and Padaki; Alman and Rao; Alman and Chen; Zongpeng Li
and Baochun Li; and the other authors credited where their results are used in the README. Dugongue (#5813, #5815),
ShikeChen01 (#634) and philippeVV (#2838) on the hub.

Substantial AI assistance: the map, the check and the text were written by AI agents (Anthropic Claude) under my
direction. No independent human review is claimed. Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

In README (`## Open next questions`) and `TASK.json`. The smallest useful follow-ups: compare the preprint's
interpolating polynomial with Alman–Williams's at equal degree (share of entries each gets wrong); test one gadget
that splits the vector tables of an Orthogonal Vectors instance across low-degree vertices, so the preprint's
tensor-contraction theorem applies; re-read the map when the working group reports.
